transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well... I guess what brings me in is, I just don’t have the push in me like I used to. I used to go to choir, and I had my quilting things, and I’d visit folks, you know, people I know are expecting me or wondering where I’ve been. But most days now I just end up sitting at home with the TV on low, not even really watching it much. I’ll think, “I should get up, I should call somebody, I should go,” and then I just don’t. It’s like the get-up-and-go part of me is missing.
How long have you been feeling this way, without the push to do things you used to enjoy?

It’s been… I’d say it started after I retired from the school office. That was a little over two years ago now. At first I thought it was just because my days weren’t structured the same way anymore, you know, not having to get up and be somewhere, answer the phone, see the children and the teachers coming through. But little by little it just sort of built up, and now it feels like it’s been going on for quite a while.
Have you found yourself feeling guilty or like you’re not worth much lately?

I don’t know that I’d say guilty, exactly. I mean, I get disappointed with myself sometimes, because I’ll look around and think, “Well, you could’ve done something today,” or I’ll remember I didn’t call someone back, and that doesn’t feel good. But feeling like I’m not worth anything… no, I don’t think that’s how I’d put it. It’s more like I’m stuck or slowed down, not that I’m a bad person.
Have you noticed that you no longer enjoy things that used to bring you pleasure, like your quilting or choir?

Yes… yes, I have noticed that. It’s not that I hate those things now, exactly. I still know quilting is something I used to love, and choir too — I used to look forward to seeing everyone and singing with the group, and with quilting I could sit there and work on a piece for hours and feel like I’d done something good with my hands. But now I just don’t seem to have the push to start.

I’ll think about it, you know. I’ll see my quilting things sitting there, or I’ll remember choir is happening, and I know people might be expecting me or wondering why I’m not there. Same with visiting folks. I know I should go, and part of me still thinks those are good things. But most days I end up just sitting at home with the TV on low, not even paying much attention to it. It’s like the wanting doesn’t turn into doing.
Would you say that most days you feel down or sad, like you're in a low mood for much of the day?

I’m not sure I’d call it sad, exactly. I mean, I’m not walking around crying all day or feeling like… like a heavy sadness in the way people talk about. Some days I do feel kind of flat, or quiet inside, if that makes sense. I’ll sit there and realize the morning has gone by and I haven’t really felt much of anything one way or the other.

There are times I get a little blue, especially when I think about how I used to be busier or more involved, but most days it’s more like I’m just dulled down. Not cheerful, but not exactly crying-sad either. So I don’t know how to answer that cleanly. It’s more of a low, empty sort of feeling than a strong sadness.
Do you feel physically slowed down or like even small tasks take a lot more effort than they used to?

Yes, I think that’s a fair way to put it. It’s not always that my body feels heavy like I can’t move at all, but even little things feel like they take a lot more push than they used to. Like getting ready to go to choir, or pulling out my quilting, or even just deciding to go visit somebody — I’ll know I ought to do it, and I’ll know people may be expecting me, but somehow I just don’t get myself moving.

Most days I end up staying home with the TV on low, and I’m not even really watching it closely. It’s just there. And I’ll sit and think, “Well, you could get up now,” or “You could at least start one small thing,” but then it feels like there’s this big space between thinking it and actually doing it. So yes, small things do feel like more effort now, even when they’re things I used to care about.
Have you noticed that you feel more tired than usual, even if you haven’t done much, or that you just don’t have the energy to do things you used to handle easily?

Yes… I think so, though I don’t always know if “tired” is the exact word. It’s more like I just don’t have the push in me. I can be sitting there at home, and I haven’t done anything strenuous, nothing that should wear me out, but the thought of getting up and going to choir, or pulling out my quilting things, or going to visit folks feels like too much to start.

And that’s really what brings me in, I guess. Those used to be things I could handle, things I cared about. Choir was part of my week, and quilting too, and visiting people — I knew where I was supposed to be and I’d go. Now most days I just stay home with the TV on low. Sometimes I’m not even really watching it, it’s just on, and I sit there knowing people may be expecting me, or wondering where I am, and I still don’t get moving. So yes, it feels like my energy for those things is just… not there like it used to be.
Would you say that you’ve lost interest or pleasure in most of the things you used to enjoy, not just some of them?

Yes… I think it’s more than just one thing. I don’t know if I’d say there’s absolutely nothing I could enjoy, because sometimes if someone gets me started I might feel a little bit of something, but left on my own, I don’t go toward those things anymore.

Choir used to matter to me. I used to know what day it was by that, almost, and quilting too — I could sit with the pieces and feel like I was doing something useful and nice. And visiting folks, that was just part of life. Now what brings me in is that I just don’t seem to have the push for any of it. I’ll think, “You should go, they may be expecting you,” or “You could at least get your quilting out,” and then I don’t.

Most days I just sit at home with the TV on low. It isn’t even that I’m enjoying the TV so much. It’s just on, and the day goes by. So yes, I guess the interest or pleasure has gone down in most of the things I used to do, or at least I don’t feel drawn to them like I used to.
Would you say that you’ve lost interest or pleasure in almost all activities, even ones that used to be a big part of your life?

Yes… I suppose I would say that, at least for the things that used to be the main parts of my life. I don’t know if “almost all activities” is the exact way I’d put it, because I still sit with the TV on, but I’m not really getting pleasure from it. It’s just on low in the background, like company almost, and then the day goes by.

What brings me in is I just don’t have that push I used to have. Choir used to be important to me — I knew people there, and I knew they might be expecting me. Quilting too, I used to feel like, well, I was making something and using my hands. And visiting folks, that was just something I did. Now I think about doing those things, and I may even know I should, but I don’t get myself started.

So yes, it feels like the interest or the pull toward those things is mostly gone. I’m not saying I hate them now, exactly. It’s more like they’re far away from me somehow, and I stay home instead.
Would you say that you’ve lost interest or pleasure in almost all activities, even ones that used to be a big part of your life?

Yes… yes, I think I would. I know I may have already said it, but that’s really the thing that’s been worrying me. It isn’t just that I missed choir once, or I didn’t feel like quilting one afternoon. It’s more like the part of me that used to get up and go do those things just isn’t there the same way.

Choir used to be a real part of my life. I knew the people, and I knew they expected me, and I used to just go without making such a big battle of it in my head. Quilting was the same way — I’d get my things out, sit with it, work on it little by little. And visiting folks too, I used to do that. Now I can sit there at home and think, “Well, they may be wondering where I am,” and still I don’t get up.

Most days I just have the TV on low. Sometimes I couldn’t even tell you what’s on. It’s just noise in the room, and I sit there, and the day kind of slips away. So yes, I’d say I’ve lost interest or pleasure in most of the things that used to matter to me. It’s not that I decided to stop caring exactly… it’s more like I don’t have the push anymore.
Would you say that your low mood and loss of interest in activities have been present for most of the day, more days than not, for the past two years?

Yes… I think so. It’s hard for me to put exact days on it, because one day runs into the next sometimes, but this has been building since I retired from the school office, and that was a little over two years ago now.

At first I thought maybe it was just the change, you know, not having to get up and be somewhere, not having the same routine. I told myself, well, anybody would feel a little lost after stopping work. But it didn’t really lift. It sort of settled in more and more. Some days are not as bad as others, but more often than not, it’s there most of the day — that low feeling, and not wanting to start the things I used to do. So yes, I’d say it’s been going on about that long.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight lately, like losing or gaining a lot without trying?

I don’t think so… not that I’ve noticed in any big way. I mean, I don’t weigh myself every day or anything like that. I’ll notice if my skirt feels tight or loose, or if something doesn’t button the same, and I haven’t had that kind of change where I thought, “Oh my goodness, I’ve lost a lot,” or “I’ve gained a lot.”

My eating is… well, it can vary some, just depending on the day, but I can’t say there’s been a big weight change without trying. Nothing someone has pointed out to me either, at least not that I can remember. So I’d say no, not significant.
